findings.mechanism: Every process_batch creates a CheckpointWatcher and subscribes it to registry._LISTENERS['checkpoint'] (ingest/registry.py:3,7). Nothing ever unsubscribes (no unsubscribe API; fire() does not drop listeners; only test-only reset() clears). Each watcher holds a 'marks' dict (ingest/watchers.py:8) with one entry per known sensor (up to 64), ~790 B, plus a sensors tuple and label, so retained memory grows linearly with batches.
findings.cause: per-batch listener subscribed to a module-global registry and never removed after the checkpoint fires
findings.evidence: Ran load.run under tracemalloc: listener_count('checkpoint') equals the number of batches (2000/6000/14000 over cumulative runs); watchers.py:8 is the top allocation site, 3 MiB at 2000 batches, 9 MiB at 6000 and 21 MiB at 14000, ~790 B per watcher, surviving gc.collect().

findings.mechanism: Module global parser._newest points to the latest Record, and each Record.previous (set at parser.py:27, models.py:10) points to the one before it. This builds an unbounded singly linked chain of every Record ever parsed, with its tags tuple and strings. Only delta needs previous.value, so the back-reference isn't needed.
findings.cause: back-reference 'previous' on Record chains all records together from a global head
findings.evidence: After parse_batch over 4000 batches with no pipeline or registry involved, tracemalloc held ~3.1 MiB after gc.collect(). Walking parser._newest.previous gave a chain length of 8000, which is every record parsed (2 per batch). Record, tag tuple and line-split allocations at parser.py:16/24/25 grow linearly.

findings.mechanism: Pipeline.per_sensor is a dict keyed by sensor, overwritten on each record.
findings.evidence: Reviewed the code: keys are the sensor ids, and load.py uses only 64 sensors, so the dict stays at <=64 entries. It did not appear among the growing allocation sites in tracemalloc.
findings.discriminator: The dict is keyed by sensor and values are overwritten, so its size is bounded by the number of distinct sensors (64), not by batch count. In production the bound depends on the sensor population being finite.
